cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's tax machine prepare Forms 1099-NEC for HANGS.
First, it checks each vendor's W-9 tax form.
Next, the year's 134 payments, about $2.3 million. A 1099-NEC reports what each independent contractor was paid.
Now it checks the IRS rules online: all ten confirmed, two questions left for a person.

Then it sorts every payment, leaving nine contractors. Corporations, materials and card payments are left out. One vendor never gave a tax ID, so 24 percent is held back for the IRS: that's backup withholding.
Eight checks pass, with no differences.
Last, it writes the draft forms and their workpapers.

All done. Nine draft forms report $708,088 paid to contractors. Five items stay open, including a tax ID that doesn't match IRS records, $1,344 of withholding never taken, and a worker who may be an employee. A person reviews and e-files by February 1; nothing is filed yet.
